description: One row per distinct value of Fabric Master.fabric -- the catalogue's own construction vocabulary, mirrored. Counts and weights are measured from Fabric Master, not asserted. `family_key` groups constructions for the substitutability graph the cost optimiser uses.

fields.description: Exactly as stored in Fabric Master.fabric. This is what the catalogue calls the construction, so it is what a rule names and what the optimiser matches.
fields.label: Construction

fields.description: The knit family this construction belongs to (jersey, rib, pique, interlock, terry, fleece, waffle, trim, ...). Several constructions can share a family; substitutability between families comes from surplus_recommender.RELATED_FAMILIES.
fields.label: Family

fields.description: Untick for values that are not real constructions. Fabric Master holds a handful of yarn-process annotations in this column (EL, COMPACT, EL COMPACT) and one stray mill code; they name how the yarn was spun, not what was knitted, and are never suggested.
fields.label: Active

fields.description: A finding rather than yardage -- collar, cuff, tape, drawcord, dori. Never substituted for fabric, and never substituted across kinds.
fields.label: Is Trim

fields.description: Fabric Master rows carrying this construction.
fields.label: Catalogue Rows

fields.description: Lightest weight the catalogue knits this construction at. Zero means no row carries a weight (true of every trim).
fields.label: GSM Min

name: Fabric Construction Family
